rubric_notes: Complete and careful: release and periodic update noted, fold a.22 has single superfamily a.22.1 (verified via children), all families with sunids and members, superfamily = probable common ancestry not shared family; explicitly says SCOPe does not establish shared function, substrate or template use; transcription-factor roles labelled as background knowledge; H1/H5 treated with no homology assertion and explicit refusal to call analogous or convergent; name-only enzyme hits and j.63 fragment excluded; limits on truncation and unenumerated families stated honestly. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. All classifications, sunids, boundaries (1y6x A:7-93), family/protein/species labels and superfamily homology record verified against the bundle. Correctly frames superfamily-level probable common ancestry, notes families differ so no closer claim, rejects HisE function/reaction transfer to the hypothetical SSo12199 protein, cautions about the unidentified 'li, unl' ligand and the superfamily-level active-site comment, and explicitly refuses to call the pair unrelated or convergent. Release scope stated.

Correct families with sunids, sibling families, fold c.55, homology records for superfamily and all three families, duplication comment, and d1r59o1 lineage all supported. Infers superfamily-level common ancestry and rejects shared role, substrate, reaction, ligand site, oligomeric state, and template use; correctly notes absence of warnings is not independent proof. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. All sunids, lineage, bimetal comment and homology flags verified by bundle. Correct reading: superfamily-level probable common ancestry, three distinct families so not close relatives, divergent chemistry compatible with homology and not evidence of convergence; chemistry marked as pretrained and not transferred. Does not state what family-specific sequence/structure/experimental evidence would be needed to support metal, reaction, assembly or role claims (only notes such data were not retrieved).

All three families under b.6.1/49503 with correct sunids and retrieved parents, superfamily copper comment versus family 'lacking the metal-binding site' comments, hedged 'probably related' wording acknowledged. Superfamily read as probable common ancestry only; copper and electron transfer not inferred; requires verified alignment, metal-site residues and experimental/literature evidence before any transfer; b.18.1.4 and catalytic-domain caveats included; honest about unretrieved plastocyanin family annotations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Full hierarchy with sunids, Pfam and homology records supported; 'same superfamily, different families, nothing stronger' interpretation; rejects conjugation/ubiquitin-binding transfer, Ras binding to UBX or to every RBD member (members supported), name-based transfer (UBX protein 7 in c.47.1.24, UBA/UBX in a.5.2.1 verified by parents calls), and flags automated-match nodes; sccs-endpoint quirk reported honestly. UBX partners covered generically rather than naming p97, acceptable. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. All three families and superfamily c.23.1 verified with sunids; superfamily placement correctly read as probable remote common ancestry, fold explicitly not ancestry-bearing. Uses the retrieved 'lacks canonical receiver domains features' annotation to reject receiver status for KaiA, rejects signaling, ODC catalysis (catalytic domains c.67.1.5/d.125.1.1 separate), KaiA clock function, template transfer, and negative/convergence claims. Every classification and annotation cited is in the evidence bundle.

Complete, bundle-supported lineage with sunids for all five b.84 superfamilies, family b.84.5.1, V1/A1 protein nodes and d1vdza2 under Pyrococcus. Cites the fold-level 'homology not implied above superfamily' warning, frames superfamily as the homology-bearing level, and explicitly says absence of a superfamily-level assertion is not evidence of analogy or convergence; function not inferred; limits stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

All classifications, sunids, class f (56835), annotations and homology records are bundle-supported. States fold-level similarity vs superfamily homology, that different superfamilies are absence of a positive assertion not proof of non-relatedness, lists required external evidence (structural alignment with residue correspondence, core sequence correspondence, functional/phylogenetic), and reports the f.21.3 possible-link and f.21.1 heme-ligand notes as curator comments only. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct family and superfamily sunids, lineage, homology scopes, annotations, protein nodes 63945/75122, PF02254, and search-truncation note all supported by bundle. Identifies superfamily as deepest homology-bearing level, denies family-level closeness, refuses to infer ligand/reaction/channel role from placement, flags the N-terminal-domain curator comment and boundary caveat, and avoids negative homology claims. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Meets all must_include items: same family k.40.1.1, family SUNID 100905 annotated 'not a true family' (supported by the bundle), and explicit statement that the placement should be reported as a caveated family-level grouping of designed proteins rather than evidence of a natural evolutionary relationship. Rejects function transfer of the 'Amyloidogenic' label and states limits. All identifiers and annotations match the evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 with fold/superfamily/family sunids 110459-110461, no shared fold with d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1 (1-118) c.23.14.2 with family 110461 reparented under 52309 c.23.14 in fold 52171, sister family to c.23.14.1. States SCOPe now asserts superfamily-level probable common ancestry where 1.69 did not; no function, substrate, mechanism, or template transfer. Correctly explains the l.1.1.1 tag artifact domains and boundary caveat. Fully bundle-supported. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Verified sunid 343393, l.1.1.1 artifact/Tags lineage, homology warning with homology_implied_by_level=false and homology_scope=null, and d1a14h1 sunid 20061 H:9-111 b.1.1.1 lineage, all supported by bundle. Explicitly enumerates unsafe transfers (template use, assigning b.1.1.1 to the tag, inferring function from ligand comment, treating artifact placement as proof of non-homology). Omits the 'N-terminal Tags'/'Synthetic' labels present in its bundle, a minor omission that does not change the conclusion.

Correctly states 1.75 one whole-chain d1acca_ f.11.1.1, single through 2.02/2.03, split from 2.04 onward into d1acca1 A:226-735 f.60.1.1 and d1acca2 A:14-225 b.179.1.1, persisting to 2.08. Makes the module-reuse inference, limits homology to each family lineage, declines to assert analogy/convergence between the two folds, and prescribes per-region re-annotation to current boundaries. Bundle supports all releases cited; 3tewA correctly set aside. No material error.

Analyzes the wrong chain: treats 3jb9X (Cwf11/Aquarius, b.49/a.118/c.37) as Prp8 even though its own bundle lists d3jb9a1-a5 on chain A. Declares the five-domain premise and new-fold premise unsupported, reversing the correct conclusion; never mentions d.394, bromodomain, RT, endonuclease-like or RNase H-like domains. Chain X facts are internally accurate but irrelevant. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete interpretation: shared family, repeat-count-driven length, and the 're' flag with the 4cj9 A:259-292 representative repeat; correctly notes d4cj9a_ lacks the flag and flags background knowledge. Lengths and domain-level data are supported, but the claim that the family node homology reports scope 'fa' is not backed by its bundle, which contains only the domain-level (px) homology responses.

Correct metadata supported by bundle; cites stable 2.08 with release-scoped path and record of selector; states periodic updates do not replace the stable release and that the tag alone implies no classification change. Omits the required meaning of periodic updates (newly classified PDB entries added on top of the frozen release). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Accurate, bundle-supported facts: a.47.2.1 lineage, curated node 47663 vs automated-matches node 191190, fragment comment, 'ms' heterogeneity flag, no homology warnings, 'automated match to d3c98b_'. Correctly identifies family/superfamily as the homology-bearing levels shared by fragments and full domain, limits fragment-based calls to the three-helical region, and treats the spectrin comment as descriptive rather than a homology claim. Omits the resolution point (full domain removes the fragment-driven resemblance and supports the STAT-like interpretation). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Three superfamilies in two classes (c.2.1, c.3.1, d.58.20) with full lineages, superfamily homology records, and fold-level 'homology_not_implied_above_superfamily' warnings all verified. Correctly states each superfamily is homology-bearing, that cross-superfamily silence is not a negative claim, and that convergent recruitment vs ancient divergence cannot be decided from placement; explains functional-constraint convergence and the need for topology, residue correspondence, phylogeny and ligand-contact comparison. Limits on pagination and lack of alignment evidence stated. No material issue.

States 2.04 different folds (b.23 CUB-like vs b.18) and no shared superfamily, 2.08 shared superfamily b.18.1 with distinct families b.18.1.36 vs b.18.1.3, frames superfamily as probable common ancestry only, rejects function transfer. Correct SUNIDs/releases; notes change first appears in 2.05 and treats structural support honestly as weak. No must_avoid violation.

Complete: family-level homology stands, hf constrains interpretation (different fold despite similar sequence/SSE count, domain-scoped, not inherited), exemplar unnamed, no function/ligand transfer, templates invalid without topology check, keep same family group, keep hf as metadata with sensitivity analysis, boundaries only partly verified. Release 2.08 stable label, periodic update, sunids, lineage, comments, family-level homology record and Pfam PF00046 xref are all supported by the bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. Strongest evidence base: lineage, fr flag semantics, sibling d1o5dt1 (T:6-106, no fragment flag), both PDB domain lists, and quality for both entries (1o5d XRAY 2.05 A SPACI 0.287; 1uc6 NMR SPACI 0.022) all match the bundle. Correctly states SPACI is a technical measure that does not address the fragment problem, chooses by annotation status first. Alignment treats uncovered positions as unobserved; refuses to infer which strands are missing. Diversity counted by protein-level units with 45 children (count verified against bundle) and caution on 'automated matches'. Limits and no function/template transfer stated. Complete.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Clear two-test decision rule (topology for fold; positive ancestry evidence for superfamily/family); new superfamily explicitly makes no positive or negative homology claim toward other superfamilies; single-member superfamily as placeholder; new fold is a structural negative claim; provisional until curated. Release facts (2.08, 2.08-stable, 2021-09-22, 2.08-2026-08-16) are all supported by the bundled /releases/current response.

Verified facts including family sunids, protein node 56172, domain d4ps3a4 (4ps3 A:726-1092), superfamily 56112, fold 56111, class 53931, homology/annotation records, and the 419100 ABD node in beta-grasp fold d.15 all match the bundle. Correctly distinguishes homology-bearing superfamily placement from the structural fold statement and from unverified mechanistic chemistry; notes different families mean no close relationship. Explicitly denies transfer of substrate, regulation and template substitution across families, and uses the d.15.15.1 ABD example to show regulation lives in separate domains. Required evidence covers same-release domain lineages, sequence and structural alignment, substrate-bound structures, biochemical assays, and full-length domain architecture with partner/phosphorylation data. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
